subject: Operational carve-out request — colocated edge & customer KMS (Peridot Biotech)
messages:
From: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@peridotbio.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Operational carve-out request — colocated edge & customer KMS

Sofia / Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. As discussed on the call, Peridot is about to move our inference gateway into a colocated cage (managed by our ops team) and will continue to use our on-prem HSM-backed KMS for key operations. During load tests last week we observed intermittent KMS callouts adding 150–500ms to token generation in some traces; those spikes directly impacted our 99th percentile tail.

We understand Redwood’s standard Private SLA assumes the control plane & KMS are customer-managed for Private deployments, but we need an explicit carve-out that:
- excludes KMS-induced latency spikes from Redwood SLA breach calculations when the KMS request latency exceeds a defined threshold, and
- allows Peridot to be responsible for remediation up to our network edge before Redwood’s fallbacks kick in.

Can you share sample contract language you’ve used for similar cases, and a short list of observability & evidence we should provide (trace samples, timestamps, router counters)? I attached the network diagram and a few traces from Aug 7.

We’d like to move quickly — procurement needs target language for the purchase order by next week.

Thanks,
Aaron
Aaron Cole
VP of Infrastructure, Peridot Biotech
aaron.cole@peridotbio.com
+1 415-555-0142

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@peridotbio.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operational carve-out request — colocated edge & customer KMS

Aaron — thanks for the detail and the attachments. Looping in Naomi and Karthik to propose contract wording and the runbook we’d need. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- When you say "KMS callouts adding 150–500ms," is that service-to-service RTT from the inference host to your KMS endpoint?
- Do you have an SLA or SLO for your KMS from the HSM vendor or carrier?
- Can you provide flow-level logs for a sample outage (we only need a few 1–2 minute extracts) and a mapping of which inference nodes are in the cage?

Prelim next steps we suggest:
1) Redwood drafts a limited operational carve-out clause that enumerates specific metrics and evidence required to invoke it.
2) Peridot provides the trace slices + network diagram (attached — thanks).
3) We agree an observability set (trace IDs, packet counters, KMS call latency histograms) and a remediation window — e.g., Peridot must remediate or open a vendor ticket within X hours.
4) If remediation does not occur within the window, Redwood’s standard SLA remediation & fallback (including temporary routing to a hosted model) will apply.

I’ll ask Legal for a short-form redline. Naomi — can you draft suggested contractual language and a minimal evidence checklist? Karthik — can you confirm whether this requires adjustments to our monitoring hooks for the Private runtime (metric names we should expect from customer traces)?

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@peridotbio.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operational carve-out request — colocated edge & customer KMS (proposed language + runbook)

Aaron / team — attaching a proposed carve-out redline (redline-proposed-carveout.docx) and a short operational runbook below. Key points condensed for the PO:

Proposed contract excerpt (plain language):
"Where Customer elects to operate Customer-managed cryptographic key services or colocated edge network components that perform cryptographic operations ("Customer KMS"), Redwood’s Platform SLOs for request latency and availability shall exclude periods where Customer KMS request latency to the Redwood runtime exceeds 200 milliseconds median and 350 milliseconds 95th percentile, provided that Customer supplies contemporaneous evidence described in the Evidence Requirements section. Exclusion may be invoked only after Customer has: (a) notified Redwood within 1 hour of observing the condition, (b) opened a vendor remediation ticket where applicable within 4 hours, and (c) provided the evidence set within 12 hours. If remediation is not completed within 72 hours, standard Redwood SLA remedies shall apply."

Evidence requirements (minimum):
- Trace slices from Redwood request IDs showing KMS call timestamps and durations (UTC).
- Router interface counters (1-minute samples) for the affected time window.
- KMS vendor ticket ID or HSM vendor acknowledgement (if available).
- Mapping of inference host IDs and IPs collocated in the customer cage.

Operational runbook (summary):
- Customer declares KMS-induced exception via support portal with trace IDs.
- Redwood validates artifact authenticity and correlation to platform request IDs within 8 business hours.
- If validated, the incident window is excluded from SLA calculation for uptime/latency for affected hosts.
- If customer remediation not initiated, Redwood may enable temporary fallback routing to hosted models for impacted tenants; this will be billed per standard usage rates.

Monitoring/tech notes for Karthik: we will need the customer to provide the KMS latency histogram and trace IDs prefixed with the Redwood request id tag. Karthik, suggested metric names: customer.kms.request_latency_ms and customer.edge.packet_drop_1m. Also recommend we add a short API endpoint to accept signed trace bundles for validation.

Aaron — if these thresholds look reasonable, please confirm and we’ll push to Legal for the PO clause. If you want the 95th percentile to be a higher bar we can discuss adjustments, but these thresholds map to similar carve-outs we’ve accepted with other biotech customers.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: redline-proposed-carveout.docx (contains contract text with tracked changes)

From: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@peridotbio.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operational carve-out request — colocated edge & customer KMS (ack)

Naomi / Sofia — this looks good and pragmatic. The 200ms / 350ms thresholds align with our vendor baseline. We will:
- Confirm the vendor ticketing SLA and attach the vendor ticket IDs when we submit evidence.
- Provide the requested trace slices and router counters by EOD tomorrow.

Please route the redline to our procurement contact (procurements@peridotbio.com) and copy me. Once Procurement has the PO language I’ll push for a signed PO next week. If you can also include the brief fallback billing note (estimated incremental cost if Redwood routes to hosted models during remediation), that will help our finance review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Aaron
Aaron Cole
VP of Infrastructure, Peridot Biotech
